definition: An alignment paradigm that trains models to critique and refine responses using a specified set of behavioral principles rather than direct human annotation.
details: Constitutional AI operationalizes harmlessness and helpfulness training by employing automated model supervision, removing human annotators from exposure to toxic red-teaming vectors while producing scalable supervision signals.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Think of it as the quiet rule that a tool should be useful without being dangerous. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” That deliberate caution is Constitutional AI.

citation.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
